svg.title: Failure recovery runbook for server logic
svg.desc: A six-step loop. One, detect: a user error dialog, a failed system job, an alert or missing data. Two, classify by asking whether users are blocked right now. If a synchronous step blocks saves, contain first: disable that one step, record who and when, and tell the service manager which rule is off. If an asynchronous subscriber fails, users are not blocked: leave it running or disable it, and note that events are waiting to be replayed. Three, diagnose with evidence: the error with the Prefer header for annotations, trace logs switched to All for a short time, the system job message, Application Insights, the registration compared with the manifest. Four, fix forward: reproduce with a failing test, correct, release a higher version through the pipeline; never edit Production with the Plug-in Registration Tool. Five, recover data: because the logic is idempotent, re-raise events or re-run operations for the affected rows. Six, restore and learn: enable the step, set trace logging back to Exception, add the test and update the runbook.
svg.text: Runbook: contain first when users are blocked, then diagnose, fix forward, recover, restore
Error dialog on save • failed system job •
alert • data that should exist does not.
Note time, user, record, exact message.
Maker portal Turn off, or statecode 1 on the step row.
Never unregister, never import an old solution.
Record who, when, which rule is now OFF.
Tell the service manager what is no longer checked.
The user's operation is committed. Failed jobs stay in
Optionally disable the subscriber to stop new failures.
Note which events must be replayed later.
3. Diagnose with evidence, not by guessing
Error with Prefer: odata.include-annotations="*" • trace log set to All for minutes, not days • system job message •
Application Insights • registration (lesson 68, request 2) compared with cedar-steps.json • what changed in the last release?
